title: PlaybookNarration
description: The strict JSON contract a constrained narrator (default Claude) must satisfy for one at-risk account (FEAT-6, #397; part of the native distributed accelerated compute pass for UC-1 churn — #264). The narrator is a Customer-Success strategist that writes the narrative and selects the play from the provided signed drivers — but it NEVER invents numbers: the churn probability, ARR, save-rate, and expected-retained-value priority are computed deterministically in code and are deliberately absent from this schema, so the narrator physically cannot change them. Validated at the boundary (the LLM/API response enters here) with the pboettch draft-07 validator, mirrored embedded in src/core/ml/playbook.cpp, the same pattern as the Run record; on any validation or semantic failure the playbook falls back to the deterministic rules engine so it always runs offline. See docs/playbook.md and docs/use-cases/uc1.md (4.6).

account_id.description: The account this narration is for — must echo the requested account_id (a mismatch fails the boundary, so a batched narrator can't cross-wire accounts).

primary_driver.description: The single dominant churn driver the narrator selected, by feature name. Must be one of the provided candidate drivers (when several conflict, prioritize involuntary/billing first).

recommended_play.description: The one primary retention play to run.

owner.description: The role that owns the play.

urgency.description: How urgently to act (a qualitative band, not a number).

diagnosis.description: A concise diagnosis of the dominant churn story, in the strategist's own words, grounded only in the provided drivers and numbers.

talking_points.description: Exactly three concrete talking points for the owner's outreach.

confidence.description: The narrator's own confidence in this play, in [0, 1]. This is a self-assessment, NOT a churn/ARR/priority metric — those are computed in code and never narrated.
